:::{#sol-direct-sum-practice}

Any $(x, y, z)$ is $(x - z, y - z, 0) + z\,(1, 1, 1)$,
with the first term in $\mathcal{S}_1$ and the second in $\mathcal{S}_2$,
so $\mathcal{S}_1 + \mathcal{S}_2 = \reals^3$.
Also, $c\,(1, 1, 1)$ is in $\mathcal{S}_1$ only if its third entry $c$ is $0$,
so $\mathcal{S}_1 \cap \mathcal{S}_2 = \cb{\vzero}$.
So $\mathcal{S}_1$ and $\mathcal{S}_2$ are [complementary](#def-complementary-subspaces) in $\reals^3$,
and $\reals^3 = \mathcal{S}_1 \oplus \mathcal{S}_2$.

:::
